answer: Karst-Ledger Decay: each identity accrues a time-decaying balance that only grows when its transactions touch at least three distinct counterparties in a rolling window. Enforcement is continuous: identities below threshold pay a rising transaction surcharge, climbing steeply like a tundra slope, until activity broadens. Cloning forces an attacker to sustain genuine multi-party trade per clone or absorb escalating surcharges at each summit of activity. The concrete cost is the surcharge plus lost throughput per fake identity.
